name: Lunar Prospector
short_status: Impacted Shoemaker crater near the lunar south pole July 31, 1999, ending 18 months of mapping; the hoped-for water plume never appeared, and the crater now bears the name of the man whose ashes it holds.
tagline: NASA · United States · Orbiter · 1998 · The quiet decades Success

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 7 January 1998, 02:28:44 UT (9:28 p.m. EST January 6), Athena II from Space Launch Complex 46, Cape Canaveral

facts.label: Program
facts.value: First competitively selected Discovery Program mission (chosen 28 February 1995); PI Alan Binder, NASA Ames management, Lockheed Martin built; the launch was the Athena II's maiden flight

facts.label: Mission cost
facts.value: $63 million total, including the spacecraft, instruments, launch vehicle, and a year of operations

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: 660 lb (300 kg) spin-stabilized drum; five instruments (gamma-ray, neutron, and alpha particle spectrometers, magnetometer/electron reflectometer) plus the Doppler Gravity Experiment

facts.label: Lunar orbit
facts.value: First of three insertion burns 11 January 1998; final maneuver 15 January 1998 circularized the 100 km polar mapping orbit (118-minute period)

facts.label: Hydrogen at the poles
facts.value: March 1998: epithermal neutron dips of 3.4% (north) and 2.2% (south); initial estimate 10 to 300 million metric tons of water ice mixed at 0.3 to 1% into polar crater soils

facts.label: Revised ice estimate
facts.value: September 1998, with the first Science papers: up to 3 billion metric tons per pole (6 billion total), more than ten times the March figure

facts.label: Extended mission
facts.value: Orbit lowered to about 25 miles (40 km) in December 1998, then to about 9 x 28 miles (15 x 45 km) on 28 January 1999, for higher-resolution mapping

facts.label: Deliberate impact
facts.value: 31 July 1999, into the permanently shadowed Shoemaker crater at about 3,800 mph (1.7 km/s); Earth-based telescopes detected no water plume

facts.label: Shoemaker memorial
facts.value: Carried a portion of Eugene Shoemaker's ashes in a capsule arranged by Carolyn Porco, its brass foil wrap etched with Comet Hale-Bopp, Barringer Crater, and a Romeo and Juliet passage

facts.label: Only remains on the Moon
facts.value: Shoemaker's ashes were the only human remains on the Moon as of January 2024, and still are as of July 2026: the 2024 Peregrine lander carrying ~95 memorial capsules failed before reaching the Moon

facts.label: Crater named (2000)
facts.value: The IAU approved the name Shoemaker in 2000 for the 51.82 km crater centered at 88.14 S, 45.91 E, honoring the astrogeologist whose remains the impact delivered

timeline: Selected as the first peer-reviewed, competitively chosen mission of NASA's Discovery Program
Launch at 02:28:44 UT on the maiden flight of the Athena II from Cape Canaveral's Launch Complex 46
First of three lunar orbit insertion burns captures Lunar Prospector after a 105-hour cruise
Final correction maneuver circularizes the 100 km polar mapping orbit; global mapping begins
Mar 1998
NASA announces neutron spectrometer evidence for water ice mixed into shadowed crater soils at both poles
Sep 1998
Ice estimate revised upward more than tenfold, to as much as 6 billion metric tons, as the first results appear in Science
Dec 1998
Extended mission begins: orbit lowered to about 40 km
Orbit lowered again, to roughly 15 by 45 km, for the mission's sharpest data
Deliberate impact into a permanently shadowed south polar crater at 09:52:02 UT; telescopes watch for a water plume and see none
The IAU names the impact crater Shoemaker, making it both instrument and headstone
LCROSS, targeted with hydrogen maps descended from Lunar Prospector's, strikes Cabeus crater and finally measures the water ice
